transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to call this course-approval meeting to order. We're here to review the proposed senior community-partnership capstone course for the fall term. As I understand it, the proposal currently describes this as a one-credit course assessed by a final reflective essay, combining supervised work with community organizations alongside academic reflection. Before we proceed, let's follow our standard round-robin checklist. I'd like to start with the faculty sponsor reporting on any pilot and instructional findings, then we'll hear from the registrar on coding and transcript requirements, and finally from the career-learning coordinator on partner scheduling and capacity constraints. Once we've covered all of those, I'll record the final approval with all required details before we submit the catalog update. Who would like to begin?

transcript.text: I'd like to begin with my pilot and instructional findings. I actually completed a six-week pilot with our community partners just this week. The pilot verified that students need 60 placement hours to meet the course outcomes. Under our college policy, which awards one credit for each 30 placement hours, this course actually requires two credits, not one. Additionally, the pilot used a faculty-reviewed portfolio as the assessment method rather than a final reflective essay. I have the pilot report finished but haven't yet attached it to the approval proposal — I'll make sure to do that after this meeting.
